name: Schlund
prior: Pink Trombone is the direct ancestor: a Kelly-Lochbaum tract, 44 cells stepped twice per sample with per-block reflection interpolation, glottal reflection 0.75, lip reflection -0.85, 0.999 loss per cell, turbulence 0.66 x noise x intensity at the constriction (V: research/src/pt_mod_Tract2.ts; VS: imaginary.org/node/1520), running as a JS AudioWorkletProcessor in the zakaton port and as a C# sample provider in lostmsu's mod (V: pt_zakaton_README.md; VS: awesome.ecosyste.ms lostmsu/pink-trombone-mod); it is a mouse/touch toy, not a note instrument. 'Mouth Play' is announced as a 'new instrument - vocal tract simulation' on Gearspace (VS: gearspace.com/threads/...1387497, fetch blocked - platform and date unknown). iZotope VocalSynth 2 Biovox is 'inspired by articulatory synthesis', estimates a tract from input audio, MIDI mode exists (VS: splice.com vocalsynth-2 guide; native-instruments.com vocalsynth); SocaLabs Voc = glottis + tract, vowels only (VS: plugins4free.com/plugin/2834); Plaits speech engine = LPC/SAM word banks (V: mi_plaits_speech_engine.cc, mi_plaits_sam.cc); Chipspeech, VocalTractLab (A, research tool); JOS 'Singing Kelly-Lochbaum Vocal Tract' (VS: dsprelated.com pasp). Myzel: Stimme = 5-vowel formant chorus, no consonants. Rare: the tract is well known, a pitched touch instrument with syllables per Puls hit was not found.
costNotes: Worklet only (sample-level ladder). Measured (M: sim/eng_sld_cost.js, Node 22 x64, PT-style loop with typed-array state, one turbulence injection, crude glottal pulse): 24 cells x 1 step = 131 ns/sample = 0.63 % core = 1.08 Nebel units for the ladder alone; 32 x 1 = 1.28; 44 x 1 = 1.68; 24 x 2 = 2.1; Pink Trombone's own geometry 44 x 2 = 3.11. Add node 0.06 + 3 params 0.09 + LF glottis table + noise + output ~0.2 -> ~1.4 at level 1 (idea's 1.2 is optimistic by ~15 %). The idea's level 3 (nose 14 cells + 44 cells x 2 steps) would be ~3.5 units - more than Gong (2.8) - so L3 should be 32 cells + nose (~2.0-2.2), not PT geometry. Cell maths checks: Delta x = c/SR = 7.1 mm at 48 kHz, 24 cells = 17 cm (= PT's 44 cells at 2 steps and 44.1 kHz, 3.9 mm each). Phone correction x1.0-1.5 (R: webaudio.md section 4): three fingers plus a lane = 5.6-8 of 14 units - the heaviest engine in the library, acceptable only because voices are few.
soundHeld: Held it is a single voice with an LF glottal pulse through a 24-cell tract: clear pitch (the glottis is a tabled pulse at f x 2^(detune/1200), so setF/Bebung are exact), and Hoehe = a vowel path uu-oo-aa-ee-ii with the constriction tightening into a fricative above 0.85. Static, a listener hears 'Stimme with one voice, thinner' - Stimme's chorus is fuller on a chord - so the held case wins only in motion (breath, nasal, the hiss at the top, the closure). 24 cells = 7 mm per cell: the constriction position steps in 7 mm units when Zunge slides, audible as formant jumps unless reflection coefficients are interpolated between cells (PT interpolates in time, not in space); vowels remain recognisable (A - PT's 44 cells are 3.9 mm and already coarse). Turbulence at one point gives sh/s/f-like noise whose level depends on the area at the constriction and jumps as the finger crosses 0.85 - needs normalisation and a soft onset. Closure (diameter -> 0) makes a reflection of +/-1 and the ladder rings numerically; clamp the minimum area and fade as PT does. Glottal pulse aliases above ~500 Hz without per-octave bandlimited tables.
soundBurst: The Puls role is the real novelty: a plosive (20 ms closure + 10 ms burst) followed by a vowel over the gate gives 'ta/ka/pa' syllables, short gate = 't', long = 'taa' - rhythmic babble no Myzel engine has, and three lanes with different vowels is a beatboxing choir. Costs 1.4 per hit for 0.2-0.5 s; at 1/16 that is fine for one lane. Risk: the same syllable every hit becomes a drum machine saying 'ta' - vary the vowel with Hoehe/vel and the plosive place (lips/tongue tip/velum) by lane.
failureModes: Heaviest engine: ~1.4 units measured (ladder 1.08 alone); PT-geometry L3 ~3.5 units is not affordable - cap L3 at 32 cells + nose.
Library reads it as 'Stimme 2'; static held notes are thinner than Stimme's chorus - the value is only in motion and in the Puls syllables.
7 mm cell quantisation: constriction position steps audibly when Zunge/Hoehe slide without spatial interpolation.
Turbulence level jumps at the fricative threshold (area-dependent); plosive closure rings numerically at area -> 0.
Glottal pulse aliasing above ~500 Hz; needs bandlimited tables per octave.
Three AudioParams + port messages must stay aligned to currentTime for the 20/10 ms plosive timing to be stable.
Chords of three mouths at 4-6 units squeeze the phone budget; voice stealing of a talking voice is very audible.
verdict: Rare: Pink Trombone and its worklet ports prove the tract and the consonants, and VocalSynth 2 / Mouth Play circle the idea, but no pitched touch instrument with plosive-vowel syllables per Puls hit was found. Worklet-only and the heaviest engine proposed: the 24-cell ladder alone measures 1.08 units, ~1.4 with glottis and node overhead, and the idea's level-3 geometry (44 cells x 2 steps) measures 3.1 before the nose - cap L3 at 32 cells. Held, it is a thinner Stimme unless the finger moves; as a Puls hit it is the only engine that can say 'ta', which is a genuine first. Build it if one worklet flagship is affordable, with spatial interpolation of the constriction, turbulence normalisation and bandlimited glottal tables; otherwise Stimme + a plosive burst layer gets 70 % of the effect at a third of the cost.
